104	/* ✅ correct */
105	color: var(--helix-color-text-neutral);
106	background: var(--helix-color-fill-primary);
107	
108	/* ❌ wrong */
109	color: #1a1a1a;
110	background: blue-600;

128

133	| `variant`   | `type`     | Visual style selector          |

142	
143	When an AI agent makes design or implementation decisions using Helix, it must validate three levels of readiness:
144	
145	1. **Can it? (Mechanical Readiness)**:
146	   - Does the generated code compile and use valid tokens (`var(--helix-color-...)`)?
147	   - Are canonical props (`onClick`, `variant`, `expanded`) used according to component contracts?
148	   - Query Helix via CLI (`pnpm helix component <Name>`) or contracts to fetch machine-readable props and types.
149	
150	2. **Should it? (Design Judgment Readiness)**:
151	   - Does the usage respect `neverUseFor` anti-patterns documented in the component contract?
152	   - Does it preserve accessibility contracts (WCAG AA, focus trapping, aria semantics)?
153	   - Are responsive constraints and layout components (`AppShell`, `TopBar`, `SideNav`) respected?
154	
155	3. **May it? (Authority & Governance Readiness)**:
156	   - **Consuming apps**: Agents MAY use core Helix components and create local custom components flagged with `// [CUSTOM] reason`.

161	
162	## Helix MCP tools (preferred when your client supports MCP)
163	
164	The repo registers a `helix` MCP server (`.mcp.json`, `pnpm helix:mcp`). Use its tools instead of reading
165	files or shelling out:
166	
167	1. `helix_list_components` — check Helix has the component before building anything.
168	2. `helix_get_contract` — exact props, accessibility and governance for the component you're using.
169	3. `helix_search_tokens` — the token for a concept ("danger background", "subtle text"); never hardcode.
170	4. `helix_validate_snippet` — run your JSX through it before writing the file; apply `fixedCode`, then
171	   fix what's left in `remainingAfterFix`.
172	
173	## Querying Helix from a terminal
174	
175	When an agent has shell access, use the read-only CLI to discover the exact Helix guidance needed
176	instead of searching source files broadly. It reads the same contracts, tokens, and patterns used by
177	the design system — it does not maintain a second copy of the documentation.
178	
179	```bash
180	pnpm helix search "confirmation dialog" --json
181	pnpm helix component Modal --json
182	pnpm helix token color.fill.primary-interactive-default --json
183	pnpm helix pattern empty-state --json
184	```
185	
186	Use `pnpm helix batch --command "component Button" --command "token color.fill.primary-interactive-default" --json`
187	when several lookups are needed. If no shell is available, consult `contracts/manifest.json`, the
188	specific component contract, and `.ai/maps/` directly.
189	
190	When no Helix component covers what you need, scaffold the custom one instead of writing it from
191	scratch — it comes with the `// [CUSTOM] reason:` header, semantic tokens, an accessible base and a
192	Storybook story whose `play` function is its first test:
193	
194	```bash
195	pnpm helix scaffold:custom UsageMeter --reason "Helix has no meter component" --dir src/custom/UsageMeter
196	```
197	
198	To install Helix AI context in your project:
199	
200	From a clone of the Helix repo:
201	
202	```bash
203	pnpm setup:ai [target-dir] [--dry-run]
204	```
205	
206	This copies AGENTS.md into your project (never overwriting a hand-edited one — it flags
207	a conflict instead) and writes a pointer file for whichever AI tool directories it finds
208	already in your project (`.cursor/rules/helix.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
209	Safe to run more than once. See `scripts/setup-ai.mjs` for exactly what it does and does
210	not touch.
211	
212	## Common mistakes (seen in real eval runs)
213	
214	These came up when an agent was asked to build with Helix without reading the contracts first
215	(`pnpm eval:generate`). Check them before writing the code:
216	
217	- **Toast needs `<Toast />` mounted once** (near the app root). `toast.success(...)` only queues the
218	  notification; with no `<Toast />` nothing appears (Helix logs a console warning). Signature:
219	  `toast.success(label, description?)` — the description can also be `{ description }`.
220	- **TopBar's slots are `start` and `end`** — not `search`/`actions`, not `left`/`right`.
221	- **Canonical prop names only** — `onClick` (not `onPress`), `expanded` (not `open`/`isOpen`),
222	  `label` (not `title`/`name`; but `Button` takes its text as children, never `label`), `checked` (not `active`/`selected`), `current` (not `active`). Full list:
223	  `.ai/maps/prop-map.md`.
224	- **Icons by reference** — `icon={IconPlus}`, never `icon={<IconPlus />}`, never a raw `<IconPlus />`.
225	
226	## What agents should NOT do
227	
228	- Use `style={{ color: '#xxx' }}` — always use token CSS variables
229	- Create a `<div>` grid without importing a Helix layout component first
230	- Use `onPress` — prefer `onClick` (prop-map canonical)
231	- Use Figma prop names directly — they may not match Helix contracts

```bash
pnpm helix token color.fill.primary-interactive-default --json
pnpm helix pattern empty-state --json
```

Use `pnpm helix batch --command "component Button" --command "token color.fill.primary-interactive-default" --json`
when several lookups are needed. If no shell is available, consult `contracts/manifest.json`, the
specific component contract, and `.ai/maps/` directly.

When no Helix component covers what you need, scaffold the custom one instead of writing it from
scratch — it comes with the `// [CUSTOM] reason:` header, semantic tokens, an accessible base and a
Storybook story whose `play` function is its first test:

```bash
pnpm helix scaffold:custom UsageMeter --reason "Helix has no meter component" --dir src/custom/UsageMeter
```

To install Helix AI context in your project:

From a clone of the Helix repo:

```bash
pnpm setup:ai [target-dir] [--dry-run]
```

This copies AGENTS.md into your project (never overwriting a hand-edited one — it flags
a conflict instead) and writes a pointer file for whichever AI tool directories it finds
already in your project (`.cursor/rules/helix.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
Safe to run more than once. See `scripts/setup-ai.mjs` for exactly what it does and does
not touch.

## Common mistakes (seen in real eval runs)

These came up when an agent was asked to build with Helix without reading the contracts first
(`pnpm eval:generate`). Check them before writing the code:

- **Toast needs `<Toast />` mounted once** (near the app root). `toast.success(...)` only queues the
  notification; with no `<Toast />` nothing appears (Helix logs a console warning). Signature:
  `toast.success(label, description?)` — the description can also be `{ description }`.
- **TopBar's slots are `start` and `end`** — not `search`/`actions`, not `left`/`right`.
- **Canonical prop names only** — `onClick` (not `onPress`), `expanded` (not `open`/`isOpen`),
  `label` (not `title`/`name`; but `Button` takes its text as children, never `label`), `checked` (not `active`/`selected`), `current` (not `active`). Full list:
  `.ai/maps/prop-map.md`.
- **Icons by reference** — `icon={IconPlus}`, never `icon={<IconPlus />}`, never a raw `<IconPlus />`.

## What agents should NOT do

- Use `style={{ color: '#xxx' }}` — always use token CSS variables
- Create a `<div>` grid without importing a Helix layout component first
- Use `onPress` — prefer `onClick` (prop-map canonical)
- Use Figma prop names directly — they may not match Helix contracts
